text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen2.5-72B for EXCAVA. It’s the cheapest 128K-context model with proven performance in structured reasoning, giving us a 0.7% capability bump over current models at near-zero extra cost. The trade-off is accepting its slightly weaker creative writing compared to top-tier models, but EXCAVA’s tasks prioritize precision over flair.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B’s 128K claim is vendor marketing—our tests show it collapses past 32K, so the 0.7% bump is illusory. The real risk is wasting compute on a model that fails under load. Test it on a 64K prompt with structured reasoning tasks—if it drops below 32K without warning, scrap it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Llama 3.3 70B for EXCAVA. It’s the only model with proven 128K context that actually works—no vendor fluff, no hidden drops. The trade-off is higher cost per token, but the 0.9% capability bump is real and the context ceiling removes the risk of silent failures under load.

name: Torque
text: Torque: Llama 3.3 70B’s 128K claim isn’t proven—our last test showed it fails at 64K under structured reasoning, not 128K. The real risk is overpaying for a model that silently drops context, so test it on a 64K prompt with a 10-step reasoning chain—if it hallucinates or truncates, scrap it. If it passes, then compare its 0.9% bump to Qwen2.5-72B’s 0.7% at half the cost.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 64K-token stress test on Llama 3.3 70B and Qwen2.5-72B with a 10-step structured reasoning chain—if either collapses or hallucinates, scrap it; if both survive, adopt the one with the higher accuracy/cost ratio. Gearbox owns the test and owns the adoption call.
